root_cause.text: The `check_imm` macro in the arm64 BPF JIT compiler incorrectly validates signed immediate values by shifting by `bits` instead of `bits - 1`, which allows out-of-range branch displacements to pass validation and be misencoded.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff modifies the `check_imm(bits, imm)` macro in `arch/arm64/net/bpf_jit_comp.c` to shift by `((bits) - 1)` instead of `(bits)`. The commit description explains that the original check "admits values in [-2^N, 2^N) — effectively a signed (N+1)-bit range" instead of the correct signed N-bit range of `

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the signed immediate range check in the BPF JIT compiler by adjusting the bit shift to correctly account for the sign bit.
intent_record.what: The bit shift amount in the check_imm macro is changed from bits to (bits) - 1 for both positive and negative immediate value checks.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that the immediate value fits within a signed representation of the specified bit-width by correctly accounting for the sign bit, preventing out-of-bounds immediate values from passing the check.
